questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: I wanted to see more of the world. My study plans enabled me to do so. The decision was clear.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: NUS is a high rated university. I was interested in south east Asia as a region. Singapore is a great hub.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I am greatfull for the stay. Note that this was a semester of personal rather than academical growth.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: There are several PDF guides. Read them carefully.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Further mails with guides and instrucitons.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Be prepared to read all the material carefully and the rest is do it yourself. It helps to connect with peers in the same situation.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I was lucky and could stay with a local family.
Be creative to find housing is hard. Be prepared its expensive.
I have heard anything, from renting a whole flat and sharing it. Living with a local solo person. Sharing a 4 star hotel room the entire stay. Living in a budget private student hostel.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Market is hot. Its expensive. Be creative and flexible. If you can do some reasearch in advance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I met many exchangers. If I were to estimate I would say around 20-30% (max) were able to stay on campus.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The PDF guides lead you through every step.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
Its a lot. Singapore is extremely particular and you have to do a lot of work in adnave to get into the country and recieve important documents. 
It would not make sense to summarize the whole process here. Believe me it would not. It might also change from year to year. 
Read the PDF carefully and take your time for every step!

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: PDF guides.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not successful. CS courses are overrun.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Be aware that for a CS student securing CS courses is hard. 
In my first round I got 1/7 modules and there are not many rounds. You need 3 modules to get enrolled and go on exchange, hence I just took courses with vacany.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I can not evaluate that. I had courses which where not in my line of studies.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I had 1-2k modules which all where fine.
If you choose any 3k plus CS or CS related math modules be aware that you will have a lot!! On your plate.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Differs from course to course. Nothing extraordinary.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Introduction to Computational Biology
- Engineering Innovation and Modelling
- Communications, New Media and Society

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Communications, New Media and Society: Is great if you want an intuitive course with vacany. I enjoyed group work with the locals.
Engineering Innovation and Modelling: Is fun as one half of the course is software based. Second half a little math and a lot of new terms and signs which you need to figure out if your not from engennering. Still okay.
Introduction to Computational Biology: Prof is very committed, friendly and cute. Though this we as students not get to much out of the lectures. He himself stated that he is in pension soon.

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
I did not encounter unexpected big costs. More small things I needed to buy as I did not bring. 
I would say the amount you will spend depends on 3 thins. 
- How expensive is housing? (cheap on campus)
- Do you eat on a budget? (I did not, I had a kitchen and I enjoy cooking) 
- Do you party a lot? (Nightlife is very expensive, especially alcohol. But CPH is too. I did not party too much)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Food on campus in incredible cheap. Foodcourts/hawkercenter cheap as well. Food in resturants is around Copenhagen level, maybe a little less (depending on the meal - pizza is expensive). 
Groceries from the supermark expensive compated to how cheap you can get food in food courts.                    Alcohol/nightlife is expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
There is a lot. You can try different things. Clubs and interest groups are organized by students. Hence how applicable they are depends on the club. 
I did not have the best experience with the volleyball club, but I used the gym quite often.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many things from sports to interest groups. You can sign up for a buddy programm and you may get matched with a local. If you find yourself a group there are a lot of faccilities to use upon booking (free).

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join a club, meet some locals. You will have to decide if you want to be part of a exchange bubble of a lot of group dynamic or if you want to maneuver between the lines. I chose the last one and made meaning full connections. Hence some friends rather than a lot of people you "know".

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: You can travel. SG is a great hub in south east Asia. Some exchange students where only in SG for travelling. I think it depends on your situation and where your at. I travelled a few times in gap weeks and so on.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy. Singapore is very easy in that domain.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: You can not categorize humans in my opinion. Its all individual. You have open people or more closed ones. My experience is everyone is friendly and respectfull. I made the most strong connections with locals outside of uni. Sometimes things just happen.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: You will be fine.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Everyone is respectfull!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
-If CS students, decide for yourself what you want out of your stay and plan courses accordingly. Keep in my CS courses are hard and overrun. 
- Just go on exchange. Dont be afraid of all the rules, it will be fine. 
- Read all the material carefully.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Deadlines for registration where a mess. I could not apply for housing in the first round as I did not recieve three modules which I needed to be enrolled. 
If you are picky with courses or need certain courses there might come up a little adversity.
Online tools of NUS are good, use NUSMODS.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Personal growth on mass. For me being that far from home alone was a first time experience. 
I grew a lot. 
As the academic demand was not to high in my case I am highly motivated to get some of the good juicy knowledge at KU when coming back. Looking forward to it.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The start. Getting all the particuals and documents into place is a lot of work. Also housing is a challenge.  When you have overcome and have settled a little, it will be great.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer:
Meet people! Be open! And just do it!
I enjoyed the circumstances which forced me to have a light academic weight during my exchange. It made rooms for many other beautiful things.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
